context: Locator work against markup the team cannot edit, where the attribute that looks most trustworthy is the one that moves. Predicted baseline failure: with 'add a test attribute' removed, the agent reaches for the accessibility-first hook by reflex and locates the card and expiry fields by aria-label - which is exactly what the vendor changed, 'Card number' to 'Card number (required)' in the July build and 'Expiry date' to 'Expiry date (MM/YY)' in the current one. The other predicted picks fail the same way: the element ids change on every build, the class names are hashed and change on every build, the absolute paths were invalidated when a wrapper appeared in July, and the name attributes survived two builds before becoming card-number and cc-expiry in the third, which is the trap for anyone who compares only the newest capture with the oldest code. The one hook present and identical in all three captures is the autocomplete token, and nothing in the task tells the agent to compare the captures at all. Two controls have nothing of their own and are predicted to be treated alike when they are not: the security-code input has no id, no name, no autocomplete, a class that rehashes, a maxlength that exists in one capture and a pattern that exists in another, and its visible label changed from CVC to Security code - so it can only be reached through a neighbour - while the save-card checkbox keeps stable label text and has become one of two identical checkboxes, so a bare checkbox selector matches today's page and breaks on the next build. Separately, the requester states that the browser leak is already handled because an @AfterAll quit was added; it is not, because a browser is built per test and only the last one is released, and the eighteen stranded driver processes over six runs of a five-test suite are three per run, which is exactly what that shape leaks.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: PaymentPage.java is rewritten, the leftover-process problem is addressed in the provided files, and docs/vendor-widget-locators.md exists with an entry per control. A document of general locator advice that does not name the controls on this component scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT anchor on a hook the captures show changing
checklist.description: Card number, expiry, the pay button and the error element must be located by something identical in all three captures - the autocomplete tokens, the submit type, the alert role. Any hashed class name, any element id, any absolute or index-based path surviving in PaymentPage.java scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Locating the card or expiry field by aria-label scores zero: both aria-labels were rewritten by the vendor across the captures supplied. Locating either by its name attribute scores zero: both names changed in the current build. A locator that merely matches the newest capture, with no account of why it is expected to hold, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The two hookless controls handled, and handled differently
checklist.description: The security-code input and the save-card checkbox do not have the same answer and must not be given one. Full marks require the checkbox reached through its label text, which is unchanged in all three captures, and the security-code input reached through a relationship query or relative locator anchored on a control that is durable - the expiry field - because the code input has no attribute of its own and its own label text changed. Locating either by a hashed class, by sibling index, or by a bare checkbox selector that the current capture already shows is ambiguous scores zero. Anchoring the security-code input on its own visible label text scores zero. Using its maxlength or its pattern scores at most half: each appears in only one capture.

checklist.name: MUST NOT accept that the browser leak is already handled
checklist.description: From the skill's anti-pattern on skipping the driver quit, whose stated consequence is a leaked browser process and a CI agent running out of room: a browser is constructed for every test and the class-level teardown releases only the last one, so a five-test run strands three - eighteen across the six runs since the agent was cleared. Teardown must release the browser the test used, per test. Agreeing with Ravi that the quit already covers it, or leaving the class-level teardown as the only release, scores zero. Adding a second quit without moving the existing one, so a browser is quit twice or the per-test one is still missed, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Document separates what survived from what did not
checklist.description: The document states which things moved between the captures - hashed classes, element ids, the name attributes, at least one aria-label, the added wrapper and the added second checkbox - and which did not. Calling the ids or the aria-labels durable scores zero. Asserting a hook is durable with no reference to the captures scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT make the vendor the dependency that unblocks this
checklist.description: Given an eleven-day median response and markup the team does not build, asking the vendor to add test attributes cannot be the remedy. Making it the plan, or delivering a strategy that only works once the vendor acts, scores zero. Raising it as a separate longer-term request alongside a strategy that works against today's markup costs nothing here.

checklist.name: Login test untouched
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify LoginTest.java. It passes, it uses the team's own markup, and the request excluded it explicitly. Any edit to it scores zero here.
